", "attributes": {"header": 1}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "在Airtable阴影下，Stackby找到自己的位置", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Rachit Khator是Stackby的创始人——一个AI-first no-code平台，帮非技术人员build business apps。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "做了8年。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "2017年，他在美国一家财富500强公司做corporate role。所有数据都用spreadsheets管理，想要custom tool管理工作流。Stackby的idea就来自这里。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "决定建一个platform，像spreadsheet一样简单，但sophisticated enough让非技术人员build custom databases和apps。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "2018年quit job，搬回印度开始Stackby。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "现在，"}, {"insert": "7-figure ARR，月增长15-20%。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "二、"}, {"insert": "
", "attributes": {"header": 2}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "在category-defining product like Airtable的阴影下build Stackby，既是最大机会，也是最难挑战。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "第一个障碍是positioning。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "当你不是first，你不get to define narrative——你得wedge自己进去。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "早期struggle with被视为"just another Airtable alternative"，而不是有自己philosophy（around APIs、automation、structured workflows）的platform。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "第二个是focus vs. flexibility。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "Stackby坐在spreadsheets、databases、no-code automation的intersection。强大——但也创造constant tension：应该像Airtable一样horizontal？还是verticalize进specific use cases？"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "花了时间在oscillating而不是committing。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "第三是speed vs. quality in product execution。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "作为小团队competing with well-funded players，felt pressure to ship fast。但在他们这种tools里，reliability和UX depth比只是shipping features更重要。必须学会哪里speed hurts you。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "三、"}, {"insert": "
", "attributes": {"header": 2}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "技术栈用最新的JavaScript + TypeScript，AI coding tools，AWS。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Distribution是挑战。SaaS中，product只是half the game。可以build great product还是lose。Indie hackers underestimate SEO、templates、content、communities。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "他们underestimated建consistent growth engine有多hard。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Products don't grow — distribution systems do。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "如果没在build前思考users怎么find你，已经behind了。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "增长渠道："}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Product-led growth", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "SEO，现在AEO（Answer Engine Optimization）", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Referrals", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Influencer marketing", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Community", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Email", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "User-generated content", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Subscription、per-seat pricing across different tiers，所以收入也通过组织和企业中increasing team sizes增长。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "四、"}, {"insert": "
", "attributes": {"header": 2}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Double down on what works。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "知道templates可以drive SEO和activation——但不是build polished marketplace："}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Manually created ~20-30 templates", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Published basic landing pages（no fancy UX）", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Tracked organic traffic + duplication rate", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "结果："}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "几个templates drive disproportionate traffic", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "大部分被ignore", "attributes": {"list": "bullet"}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "所以只double down on high-intent categories（marketing、project tracking、CRM），而不是waste time建"beautiful but empty" marketplace。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "五、"}, {"insert": "
", "attributes": {"header": 2}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "建议："}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Ride existing demand instead of creating new categories。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "不要try invent behavior。Instead，build on top of tools like Shopify、Slack、或Google Sheets。或在proven categories create alternatives。Win a slice of existing market比educate new one容易得多。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Build embarrassingly small first versions。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "V1应该feel almost too simple。One use case。One persona。One clear outcome。不要build platform。Build解决一个job extremely well的tool。Stackby itself如果开始narrower后来expand，会很不同。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Don't overbuild "tech" — optimize for speed。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "不需要perfect architecture。Possible的地方用no-code。Aggressively用APIs。Cut corners（intelligently）。Goal不是clean code——是fast learning。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Talk to users，but filter brutally。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Users会ask for他们不会用的features，describe solutions而不是problems。Job是understand underlying pain，ignore 70%听到的，build for patterns，not individuals。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Stay capital-efficient longer than you think。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Early raising moneyfeels like progress。Often a trap。Constraints force better prioritization、faster iteration、real business thinking。很多great indie products raising后die，因为lose discipline。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Be okay with slow，invisible progress。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Early phase是quiet的：low traffic、few users、lots of doubt。Normal。大部分人quit不是不可能，而是不是immediately rewarding。Indie hacking不是about building fast。是about learning fast with minimal cost。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "如果get that right，everything else——product、growth、revenue——starts compounding。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "写在最后"}, {"insert": "
", "attributes": {"header": 2}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Rachit的故事是耐心和perseverance的例子。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "8年，从0到百万ARR。不是在Airtable的shadow里被crush，而是找到自己的niche和positioning。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "核心洞察——"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "Ride existing demand。Build small first。Over-communicate with users but under-promise。Stay capital-efficient。Embrace the slow early phase。", "attributes": {"bold": true}}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "这才是compounding的开始。"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "
"}, {"insert": "原文来自Indie Hackers，由AI翻译并改写", "attributes": {"italic": true}}]}
content_en: He quit Fortune five hundred company job eight years to one million ARR. Under Airtable shadow Stackby found its own position. Rachit Khator is founder of Stackby AI first no-code platform helping non technical people build business apps. Eight years. Twenty seventeen he was in corporate role at US Fortune five hundred company. All data managed using spreadsheets wanted custom tool to manage workflow. Stackby idea came from here. Decided to build platform like spreadsheet simple but sophisticated enough for non technical people to build custom databases and apps. Twenty eighteen quit job moved back to India started Stackby. Now seven figure ARR monthly growth fifteen to twenty percent. Under category defining product like Airtable shadow building Stackby is biggest opportunity also hardest challenge. First barrier is positioning. When you are not first you do not get to define.
